correctness.rationale: For connected admissible walks the grounded Laplacian is positive definite; the Hessian of its inverse trace is strictly positive along every nonzero symmetric direction. Averaging preserves feasibility and is strict unless the walk is invariant. The even layer sector gives eigenvalues 0, x (multiplicity m-1), and (m+1)x; the odd sector gives x+2z (multiplicity m-1) and the stated two-dimensional quotient. Independently reconstructed exact gradients in holding coordinates (u,v,y) have positive shifted coefficients for m>=3. In the two-page case the reduced derivative has the stated cubic sign and the holding derivatives are strictly positive; the stationary edge point satisfies the supporting-plane inequality globally. Both choices are connected and loop-free, so the bipartite sign vector gives eigenvalue -1; lazification gives the unattained aperiodic infimum. The benchmark ratio follows from the leading terms. The fastest-mixing values can also be checked independently: SLEM is the convex norm ||P-J||, so it suffices to average; for m>=3 the star eigenvalue gives SLEM>=1-x>=1-1/m. At x=1/m and y=0 the odd-block eigenvalues lie in [1/m,2-1/m] exactly over the displayed rung interval by the two Schur-complement inequalities, and the other eigenvalues meet those bounds there. For m=2, the norm of I minus the odd block is at least its absolute off-diagonal entry sqrt(2)x, so SLEM>=max(1-x,sqrt(2)x). At x=sqrt(2)-1, setting both odd-block diagonal entries to 1 attains equality and is feasible; equality requires positive central weight. Thus the disjointness is independently established even without the historical manuscript.
residual_risks: The aperiodic infimum is not a minimum. The central edge is a shared rung, not a bridge in the graph-theoretic sense; removal leaves connected support.

value.rationale: The natural hitting-time and asymptotic mixing objectives have exact globally disjoint solutions on the same graph even though they share a deletion boundary. The all-size stochastic allocation identifies the exception and shows a genuine criterion-dependent pathology: the hitting-time optimum is periodic and becomes an unattained infimum under an aperiodicity requirement. The structural comparison is meaningful independently of the maximum-degree benchmark.
residual_risks: No claim for asymmetric stationary laws, directed kernels, lower bounds on all weights or added stochastic-step constraints.
